classification.difficultyReason: Recognise four equal-tangent pairs and reorganise the two opposite-side sums into the other pair.

content.prompt: The tangents at the four points P, Q, R and S on a circle form a quadrilateral ABCD. Prove that $AB+CD=AD+BC$.

spec.description: Tangential quadrilateral ABCD; contacts P on AB,Q on BC,R on CD,S on DA. No equality marks supplied.
spec.answerVisibility: Original supplied givens and targets only; no derived numerical values or proof conclusions.

answer.short: $AB+CD=AD+BC$. Replace each side by its two tangent segments and use equal tangents from each vertex.
answer.worked:
Tangents from each external point are equal: $AP=AS$, $BP=BQ$, $CQ=CR$ and $DR=DS$. Thus
$$\begin{align*}AB+CD&=AP+PB+CR+RD\\&=AS+BQ+CQ+SD\\&=AD+BC.\end{align*}$$
